title: A finite-presentation local approximation with unchanged closed fibre
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ and $(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be nonzero commutative local rings, and let $a:R\to B$ be a local homomorphism, meaning $a(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$. Assume $B$ is essentially of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. There exist a nonzero commutative local ring $(T,\mathfrak m_T)$, local homomorphisms $b:R\to T$ and $u:T\to B$ with $u\circ b=a$, a finitely presented commutative $R$-algebra $P$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq P$, and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $T\cong W^{-1}P$, such that $u$ is surjective and its induced homomorphism $T/\mathfrak m_RT\to B/\mathfrak m_RB$, $[t]\mapsto[u(t)]$, is an isomorphism. Here $\mathfrak m_RT$ and $\mathfrak m_RB$ denote the ideals generated by the respective images of $\mathfrak m_R$, and $W^{-1}P$ is the ring of fractions as in [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra].

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] choose a finite set σ in B such that every b admits a unit y with y and by in R[σ]. Let Q=R[X_i : i∈σ] and h:Q→B be evaluation, whose range is R[σ] by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Set q=h⁻¹(m_B), a prime ideal, and A=Q_q as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Every denominator outside q maps to a unit, so h extends to an R-algebra map v:A→B. For b choose the above y, lift y and by to s,p in Q, and note s∉q. Then v(p/s)=b, proving surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 05UV, lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-fp-over-ft, proof, polynomial-localization presentation B/J and choice of a finitely generated subideal with the same image modulo the base maximal ideal; only the approximation before applying Tag 00R7.

proof.text: Put m=m_R A and F=A/m. The localization A of a finite polynomial R-algebra is essentially of finite type. Passing to the closed fibre preserves this property: F is essentially of finite type over the field R/m_R. This is the quotient/base-change assertion in Mathlib Algebra.EssFiniteType.quotient_map, which avoids an explicit coefficient-by-coefficient polynomial quotient identification. By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], an essentially finite type algebra over a field is Noetherian; apply Mathlib Algebra.EssFiniteType.isNoetherianRing to F.

source.place: Tag 05UV, lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-fp-over-ft, proof, polynomial-localization presentation B/J and choice of a finitely generated subideal with the same image modulo the base maximal ideal; only the approximation before applying Tag 00R7.

proof.text: Let J=ker(v). The contraction of J to Q is ker(h), by the defining formula v(a/1)=h(a). The localization ideal correspondence (Mathlib IsLocalization.map_under) gives J=ker(h)A. For g:Q→A→F the image ideal g(ker h) is finitely generated by Noetherianity of F [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Since an ideal map is the span of the image, choose a finite subset of g(ker h) with the same span and lift this finite set to a finite subset s⊆ker h. Put K=(s) in Q and L=KA. Then K is finitely generated, L⊆J, and L and J have the same image in F. Pulling this equality back under A→F yields L+m=J+m. Choosing polynomial generators directly avoids a separate clearing-denominators step.

source.place: Tag 05UV, lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-fp-over-ft, proof, polynomial-localization presentation B/J and choice of a finitely generated subideal with the same image modulo the base maximal ideal; only the approximation before applying Tag 00R7.

proof.text: Take T=A/L. The map v factors through an R-algebra surjection f:T→B since L⊆ker v. This makes T nonzero, and as a quotient of a local ring T is local. The surjection f is local. Since the composite R→T→B is local, R→T is local too. These are the required local maps and their algebra-map compatibility.

source.place: Tag 05UV, lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-fp-over-ft, proof, polynomial-localization presentation B/J and choice of a finitely generated subideal with the same image modulo the base maximal ideal; only the approximation before applying Tag 00R7.

proof.text: Take P=Q/K. It is finitely presented over R because Q is a polynomial algebra on a finite set and K is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let W be the image of q.primeCompl under Q→P. Localization commutes with quotient, the general multiplicative-subset version of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient]: Mathlib IsLocalization.instQuotientIdealAlgebraMapSubmonoidMapRingHomAlgebraMap gives IsLocalization W T. Uniqueness of localization gives T≃ₐ[P]Localization W; restrict scalars to R. No prime ideal of P or denominator clearing is needed.

source.place: Tag 05UV, lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-fp-over-ft, proof, polynomial-localization presentation B/J and choice of a finitely generated subideal with the same image modulo the base maximal ideal; only the approximation before applying Tag 00R7.

proof.text: Let m_T=m_R T and m_B=m_R B. Functoriality of ideal extension gives v(m)=m_B and (A→T)(m)=m_T. Surjectivity of v and A→T identifies their inverse images with m+J and m+L respectively, equal by step 3. Injectivity of ideal contraction along the surjection A→T gives f⁻¹(m_B)=m_T. The induced map T/m_T→B/m_B is injective by this equality and surjective because f is surjective. RingEquiv.ofBijective gives the required ring isomorphism, and the defining quotient-map formula is [t]↦[f(t)].
